newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BRIDGESTONE SAYS LOCAL MARKET IS TOUGH.
newsitem.headline: BRIDGESTONE SAYS LOCAL MARKET IS TOUGH.

text.p: Tyre maker Bridgestone Australia Ltd said on Thursday its fall in first half earnings was due to softer market conditions but it was well positioned to take advantage of any general economic improvement.

The company, which is 60 percent-owned by Japan's Bridgestone Corp, said net profit in the six months to June 30 fell by 12.6 percent to A$5.27 million, citing reduced sales revenue and continuing pressure on profits.
"As in 1996, gross profits continue to be eroded by cost increases while selling prices remain static or have fallen," it said.

"Despite the reduced revenue, Bridgestone has maintained or improved its market share in all its key market segments and is ideally positioned to benefit from any improvement in general economic conditions," the company said.
It said the Australian tyre market remained intensely competitive with high levels of imports flooding the market.
Strong demand for the company's premium brand tyres helped offset the import competition.
First half sales fell by 3.3 percent to A$211.40 million, with the company reporting lower sales in all major divisions.
